items.title: ROSETTA: Efficient and Accurate Privacy-Preserving LLM Decoding via Hybrid CKKS/TFHE Evaluation
items.one_liner: ROSETTA accelerates privacy-preserving LLM decoding using a hybrid CKKS/TFHE evaluation framework with adaptive segmented lookup tables.
items.summary: Generative large language model deployment raises privacy concerns, leading to private inference frameworks based on fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), which typically suffer from high overhead during non-linear decoding operations. To solve this, researchers proposed ROSETTA, a hybrid CKKS/TFHE evaluation framework that handles heterogeneous workload patterns in the decode stage. ROSETTA introduces an adaptive segmented lookup-table protocol based on TFHE and an automatic operator-selection framework that assigns operators to CKKS or TFHE. Experiments demonstrate that ROSETTA achieves up to a 4.8x Softmax speedup and 1.5x to 2.1x end-to-end speedups over existing SOTA frameworks.
items.bottom_line: ROSETTA overcomes FHE decoding bottlenecks via hybrid CKKS/TFHE evaluation, achieving up to 4.8x Softmax speedups and 2.1x end-to-end acceleration.

items.title: CVE-2026-92580 - AVideo through 29.0 CloneSite Stored Shell Injection via SSH Password CSRF
items.one_liner: AVideo's CloneSite plugin exposes a stored shell injection vulnerability via an SSH password CSRF vector, posing an unauthenticated RCE risk for instances with enabled cron jobs.
items.summary: In AVideo through version 29.0, the CloneSite plugin contains a stored OS command injection vulnerability designated as CVE-2026-92580. The vulnerability arises because the plugin substitutes a stored SSH password into an rsync command using a plain string replacement without escaping, allowing a single quote in the password to inject arbitrary shell commands. The administrative endpoint used to write the password is protected by a CSRF defense that incorrectly evaluates loopback requests or co-hosted applications as trusted, and issues session cookies with SameSite=None. Consequently, an unauthenticated remote attacker can lure an authenticated administrator into planting a malicious payload, which is then automatically executed by the system's documented crontab.
items.bottom_line: AVideo versions up to 29.0 permit unauthenticated remote code execution via a combination of SSH password CSRF and unescaped rsync command substitution.

items.title: ThinkFlow: Self-Evolving Probabilistic Latent Memory for Lifelong Conversational Agents
items.one_liner: ThinkFlow replaces explicit textual conversational memory with a self-evolving probabilistic latent framework to enable lifelong, personalized agent interactions.
items.summary: Lifelong conversational agents typically rely on explicit textual memory pipelines that suffer from information bottlenecks and static post-deployment behavior. Inspired by human cognitive science and predictive coding, researchers propose ThinkFlow, an end-to-end latent memory framework designed to compress conversational interactions into probabilistic latent memory skills. ThinkFlow bypasses text-based storage by dynamically consolidating user states into continuous vectors without semantic interference. Utilizing a test-time evolution paradigm that couples teacher-guided latent alignment with self-supervised next-utterance prediction, the framework achieves label-free personalization across extended multi-session interactions.
items.bottom_line: Latent memory frameworks overcome the information bottlenecks of text-based conversational histories, enabling lifelong personalization for AI agents.

items.title: Understanding the (In)Security of Vibe-Coded Applications
items.one_liner: Auditing 9,041 AI-vibe-coded applications exposed that 91% contain security flaws, heavily skewed toward critical access control defects.
items.summary: A systematic study examining the security of "vibe-coded" applications—software created primarily through natural language interactions with AI agents like Claude Code and Lovable—revealed widespread vulnerabilities. Researchers audited 9,041 open-source applications and 200 deployed applications, uncovering 1,186 vulnerabilities and finding that 91.0% of audited apps contained at least one security flaw. Furthermore, 65.77% of identified issues were rated Critical or High severity, concentrated mainly in broken access control, injection, and authentication failures. These weaknesses trace back to memory, objective, and knowledge defects inherent in AI agents, demonstrating that prompt engineering and harness improvements reduce but do not eliminate these security risks.
key_facts: Applications audited: 200 publicly deployed (9,041 total collected)
items.bottom_line: Delegating application development entirely to AI agents yields pervasive high-severity security vulnerabilities that prompt engineering alone cannot resolve.
